In the Go repo at /bench/home/work (memos project), answer two questions with exact path:line citations.

Q1: Markdown processing sits behind an interface (look in internal/markdown/ — maybe an interface like markdown.Service or Parser/Renderer). Identify: (a) the interface name and path:line; (b) the concrete implementation(s) that execute at runtime and their construction site (who calls the constructor, e.g. in server.NewServer or a service init) path:line; (c) which components hold a reference to the interface (struct fields, e.g. APIV1Service, mcp server, memopayload runner). Report all with path:line.

Q2: Each memo has derived metadata computed from its content (a "payload" with tags, properties like hasLink/hasCode/hasTaskList — see server/runner/memopayload/ and proto MemoPayload). Report: (a) where the computation happens (function, path:line); (b) which operations trigger recomputation (callers: CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, the runner itself, etc. with path:line); (c) exactly what properties the computation extracts (tags, link presence, task list, code, etc. — list the fields set).

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Findings below.

## Q1: Markdown interface and wiring

**(a) Interface**
- `markdown.Service` — `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31` (methods declared at lines 33, 36, 39, 42, 45, 48, 51, 54)
- Supporting value type `markdown.ExtractedData` (Tags / Mentions / Property) — `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go:21`
- There is no separate `Parser`/`Renderer` interface. `renderer.MarkdownRenderer` (`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go:20`) is a concrete struct used internally by `RenderMarkdown`/`RenameTag` (markdown.go:250, markdown.go:451), not an exported abstraction.

**(b) Concrete implementation + construction**
- Sole implementation: unexported `service` struct — `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go:58` (wraps a `goldmark.Markdown`). No mocks/fakes implement the interface anywhere in the repo.
- Constructor: `markdown.NewService(opts ...Option) Service` — `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`; options `WithTagExtension` (line 71) and `WithMentionExtension` (line 82).
- **The only runtime construction site** is inside `NewAPIV1Service` — `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51` (built with both tag and mention extensions), assigned at `v1.go:56`.
- That call comes from `server.NewServer` — `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:76` (`apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(...)`).
- The same instance is then passed by reference into the RSS service — `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:85` (`rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService)`). So there is exactly one `markdown.Service` instance in a running server.
- Test-only second construction: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44` (assigned at line 52).

**(c) Holders of the interface**
| Holder | Field | Source of value |
|---|---|---|
| `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35` | self-constructed at v1.go:48 |
| `rss.RSSService.MarkdownService` | `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go:45` (ctor param `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go:58`, assign line 62) | injected from APIV1Service at server.go:85 |
| `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` | `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16` (ctor `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:19`) | **never constructed at runtime** — see note below |

Call sites through the interface:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` — `ExtractAll` for mention resolution
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:85` — `GenerateSnippet` (in `getMemoContentSnippet`)
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go:339` — `RenderHTML` for feed item bodies
- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:80` — `ExtractAll` for payload rebuild

**MCP does not hold the markdown service.** `mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)` (`/bench/home/work/server/server.go:92`, struct at `/bench/home/work/server/router/mcp/service.go:18`) is OpenAPI-driven over the in-process HTTP API and takes no markdown dependency.

**Dead interface methods:** `RenameTag` (markdown.go:54/425), `RenderMarkdown` (markdown.go:42/244), `ValidateContent` (markdown.go:51/349), `ExtractTags` (markdown.go:36/143) and `ExtractProperties` (markdown.go:39/193) have no non-test callers — all production paths go through `ExtractAll`.

## Q2: Memo payload computation

**(a) Where it happens**
- `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error` — `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`. It nil-initializes `memo.Payload` (line 75-77), calls `markdownService.ExtractAll` (line 80), then assigns `memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags` (line 85) and `memo.Payload.Property = data.Property` (line 86).
- The actual extraction is the single AST walk in `(*service).ExtractAll` — `/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go:356` (walk at lines 371-411).

**(b) Triggers / callers**
1. `CreateMemo` — `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (inside `CreateMemo`, declared at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`). Runs before `s.Store.CreateMemo`; note `create.Payload.Location` is overlaid afterwards at memo_service.go:112-114, since `RebuildMemoPayload` does not touch `Location`.
2. `UpdateMemo` — `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, but **only** inside the `path == "content"` branch of the update mask (branch begins at memo_service.go:439). The result is written to `update.Payload` at memo_service.go:449-450. Updating visibility/pinned/state/timestamps does not recompute the payload.
3. `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`, a batched (100 at a time, lines 29-71) full rebuild that persists via `Store.UpdateMemo` at runner.go:56.

**Important gap:** `memopayload.NewRunner` (`/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:19`) and `RunOnce` have **zero callers** in the repo — `server.NewServer`/`Server.Start` only wires `s3presign.NewRunner` / `RunOnce` (`/bench/home/work/server/server.go:162-163`). So the backfill runner is effectively dead code today; only Create and content-Update recompute payloads in a live server.

**(c) Fields the computation sets**
From `ExtractAll` (`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go:356-421`), written onto `storepb.MemoPayload` (proto at `/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto:7`):

| Field | Set at | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `Tags []string` (proto field 3, memo.proto:12) | markdown.go:377, assigned to payload at runner.go:85 | every `mast.TagNode` not nested inside a link/image (`asMemoTagNode`, markdown.go:134; guard `isTagNodeInLinkOrImage`, markdown.go:122); deduped case-preserving via `uniquePreserveCase` (markdown.go:418, 456) |
| `Property.Title` (proto field 5, memo.proto:21) | markdown.go:387 | text of the first block-level child of the document only if it is an H1 (`firstBlockChecked` logic, markdown.go:384-389; text via `extractHeadingText`, markdown.go:173) |
| `Property.HasLink` (proto field 1) | markdown.go:394 | any `gast.KindLink`. Note: bare autolinks (`gast.KindAutoLink`) are **not** counted |
| `Property.HasCode` (proto field 3) | markdown.go:397 | any of `KindCodeBlock`, `KindFencedCodeBlock`, `KindCodeSpan` |
| `Property.HasTaskList` (proto field 2) | markdown.go:400 | any `east.KindTaskCheckBox` |
| `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` (proto field 4) | markdown.go:403 | at least one `TaskCheckBox` with `IsChecked == false` |
| `Mentions []string` (in `ExtractedData` only, **not** persisted) | markdown.go:380, deduped at markdown.go:419 | lowercased `MentionNode.Username`; consumed only by `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32`, dropped by `RebuildMemoPayload` |

`MemoPayload.Location` (proto field 2, memo.proto:10) is never derived from content — it is set from the request in `CreateMemo` (`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:113`). Because `RebuildMemoPayload` replaces the whole `Property` message and preserves the `Payload` pointer, a content update keeps `Location` intact.

Downstream consumers of these fields: `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` (`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:315`, used at memo_service_converter.go:48-49) and the user stats aggregation (`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:138-152` and 254-268).
